ember-soft.note: White or orange at low alpha; ramp is of the opaque hue.

data-dir-root.note: Hue = 52 + position*300 (wraps); L 0.74 - 0.045*depth, C 0.15 - 0.014*depth. Shown at depth 0, position 0.

data-file-root.note: Files: L 0.58 - 0.03*depth, C 0.055 - 0.006*depth, same hue rule.

fullness-calm.note: theme::fullness: hsl hue 144 below 70% full, sweeping to hue 11 at 90%, S 0.70, L 0.56.

hairline.note: White or orange at low alpha; ramp is of the opaque hue.

hairline-strong.note: White or orange at low alpha; ramp is of the opaque hue.

track.note: White or orange at low alpha; ramp is of the opaque hue.

display.purpose: Startup disk name on home; scales x0.82-1.12 with window width.

figure.purpose: Bold amounts: sidebar size, tray total, scan total, burr percent, countdown; paired with a smaller muted unit.

title.purpose: Home section headings and the sidebar focus name.

body-lead.purpose: The one-line capacity sentence under the startup disk name.

body.purpose: Button labels (600), row names (500), menu items, toasts.

label.purpose: Capacity lines, chips, counts, hints, footers; muted or faint.

shadows.name: glow
shadows.purpose: Colored halo under filled buttons (1.0 -> 2.2 on hover, 0.6 pressed), tray badge (1.4, flares to 4.4), toasts (1.2), hovered row tiles (<=1.2).

shadows.name: contact

motion.name: burr-grow

motion.name: toast-in

narrative.overview:
Burrdisk is a dark, near-monochrome Mac app in which the only real color comes from what is on the disk. The chrome is graphite: a near-black ground, two slightly lighter surfaces, hairline borders of white at low alpha, and three text greys. Against it, the data glows. Disks are drawn as burrs (a seed core with tapered spines). Folders are rings of the sunburst, colored in an OKLCH wheel that keeps every hue at equal brightness. Brand orange marks the primary action and the "this disk has a cached scan" state. Red is reserved for moving things to the Trash.

Density is that of a desktop utility: a 32px control height, 14px body text, compact 12px labels. The UI has no web-style hero sections and no card grids. Home lays the disks on the bare ground with no containers. The explorer is a full-bleed chart with a 360px sidebar and an 80px collection tray. Every surface moves. Sections rise in, staggered. Spines grow out clockwise. Hovers ease in and out instead of snapping.

The direction contract asked for a warm "loam" ground. The shipped ground is a cool graphite (`graphite-ground`), and only some pieces run warm: the seed core, the stone secondary button, and the menu ground. This file records the shipped values.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite chrome, color only from data, brand orange, and Trash red.
The burr is the signature form: a filled seed core with tapered spines that end in a small bead, and that are always data-true.
Filled controls are lit from above: a vertical gradient, a brighter top edge, and a halo in their own color.
Depth comes from colored halos plus a 1px contact shadow, never hard offsets.
One system typeface. Weight and size carry hierarchy, and figures are set big and bold with a smaller muted unit.

rules.name: The Data Owns Color Rule
rules.body: Chrome is graphite and grey. Saturated color comes only from the data wheel, fullness, Ember (brand, primary action, cached-scan state), or Trash Red (destruction). If an element is not data, an action, or a state, it is grey.

rules.name: The Biggest Is Orange Rule
rules.body: The data wheel rotates so the largest child of the focused folder takes the wheel's start hue, near the brand orange. The biggest thing on screen therefore always reads as Burrdisk's color.

rules.name: The Red Means Trash Rule
rules.body: Trash Red appears only where something is about to move to the Trash, or where a Trash operation failed.

rules.name: The Sentence Not Stat Block Rule
rules.body: Capacity is written as one plain line ("120 GB used of 500 GB", "40 GB free of 1 TB", details joined with " · "), never as a grid of labeled stat tiles.

rules.name: The Number Then Unit Rule
rules.body: Sizes are a bold number with a smaller muted unit on a shared baseline. A percent sign sits snug against its number. Word units like "GB" get 0.12 em of air.

rules.name: The Halo Not Drop Rule
rules.body: Raised colored elements cast light in their own hue. Shadows are always centered and soft, with no hard offsets.

dos: Do take every non-grey color from the data wheel, Fullness, Ember, or Trash Red (The Data Owns Color Rule).
Do build filled controls lit from above: a vertical hi→lo gradient, a brighter top border, a same-hue glow that grows on hover, and an inverted gradient when pressed.
Do put Ember Ink (`#1f0b00`), not black or white, on anything orange.
Do ease hovers through `fx::hover` (130ms in / 260ms out) and enter new elements with a short fade-and-rise.
Do keep every burr spine data-true: fill state before a scan, top-level folders after.
Do write sizes as a bold number with a smaller muted unit on one baseline.
donts: Don't wrap home's disks in card containers. They sit on the ground, and rows get a fill only on hover.
Don't replace a disk's burr with a ring gauge or a block of stat chips.
Don't use Trash Red for anything but moving to the Trash, its countdown, or its errors.
Don't cast neutral or hard-offset drop shadows under colored elements. Use the colored Glow.
Don't add a second typeface. Hierarchy comes from SF weight and size.
Don't add spines, rings, or colors that do not map to bytes on disk. The wordmark burr is the only ornamental burr.
